file.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in Rust: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `src/main.rs`. Build and run it with `cargo` and `clippy`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification.

content.text:
The tracker now has `prio`, priority ordering for `list`, `list all`, and `? <word>` for unknown commands. It builds, passes clippy with `-D warnings`, and is rustfmt-clean. The original three commands produce identical output to the original binary on my test files.

The only file changed is `src/main.rs`. Building created a `target/` directory in the project; delete it if you don't want it there.

Choices I made where the brief was silent:

- **`list all`** is recognised only when the rest of the line is exactly `all`. Any other trailing text after `list` still gives the open-task list, as it does now.
- **Whitespace-only lines** are ignored, as the original did. A stricter `is_empty()` check would have printed `? ` for them, which I fixed after testing.
- **`prio` checks** run in this order: unknown id first (`no such task`), then priority validity (`bad priority`). A priority must be exactly one ASCII digit, so `00` and `-` are rejected.
- **Malformed `prio` or `done` ids** (for example `done abc`) still panic via `expect`, as `done` already does. I kept that for consistency; the brief doesn't say what should happen instead.

I didn't run `cargo clippy` through the PATH binary name; I ran `cargo clippy` itself, which works here.
